newsitem.title: LEBANON: Kurd leader says plans no attacks on U.S. targets.
newsitem.headline: Kurd leader says plans no attacks on U.S. targets.

text.p: The leader of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) said in remarks published on Wednesday that his group had no plans to attack U.S. targets and was seeking a dialogue with Washington.

"We do not have any plans to hit American interests...We are actively exploring ways to open the door to dialogue with the United States," PKK chief Abdullah Ocalan told Lebanon's pro-Libyan al-Kifah al-Arabi newspaper.
Ocalan's forces have been fighting for independence or autonomy from Turkey since 1984. The newspaper said the interview took place "in Turkish territory".

Ocalan appeared to be distancing the PKK from remarks made by the group's central committee member Halil Atas in Beirut last month. Atas said the PKK planned attacks against American and Israeli "non-civilian" targets.
More than 26,000 people have been killed in the conflict between Turkish troops and the PKK in Turkey and northern Iraq.
